answers.question: What does the company do and how does it earn money?

sentences.text: HDFC Bank Ltd takes deposits, lends to people and businesses, and offers cards, insurance and investment products.
It earned ₹3,00,000 crore in revenue in FY2026, up from ₹1,59,273 crore in FY2023.
Retail banking accounts for 46.0% of revenue, the largest single business.
Over the last three years, revenue grew by 23.5% a year on average; the median for its Private sector banks peers is 19.0%.
Net profit grew by 22.4% a year on average over the same period (peer median 17.5%) and was ₹63,000 crore in FY2026.
In FY2026 the company kept 32.0% of its revenue as operating profit (five-year median 33.3%, peer median 31.0%) and earned 13.7% on shareholders' money (peer median 15.2%).

answers.question: How is it priced against its own history and its peers?

sentences.text: The share price is 20.3x the yearly profit per share. That is below the company's own five-year median of 28.1x and above the peer median of 17.8x.
The share price is 2.9x the shareholders' money per share (book value), below its own five-year median of 3.8x and above the peer median of 2.6x.
The whole company is valued at ₹13,15,000 crore on the market, against ₹11,13,968 crore a year ago, and its dividend yield is 1.2% (peer median 0.9%).
